rules.title: Washington — Domestic Violence Leave (reasonable leave, all employers)

params.covered_reasons: legal or law enforcement assistance, medical treatment, counseling, victim services, relocation or safety planning

result.summary: All employers must allow reasonable leave (paid from accrued leave, otherwise unpaid), intermittent or on a reduced schedule, for an employee who is (or whose family member is) a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, and must provide reasonable safety accommodations. Safe leave is also a use of WA paid sick leave (RCW 49.46.210).

rules.title: USERRA — Uniformed Services Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: uniformed services (active duty, reserve and National Guard federal duty, training)

result.summary: All employers must grant unpaid leave for service in the uniformed services and reemploy the employee in the escalator position after up to 5 cumulative years of service, with no discrimination or retaliation; health coverage continues up to 24 months at the employee's expense. State-ordered National Guard duty is covered only by state law.

rules.title: Washington — State Military Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: state active duty and National Guard or state militia service

result.summary: USERRA-equivalent leave and reemployment rights for Washington residents or employees serving in the uniformed services, including state active duty. (Survey-based encoding; dates not researched.)

citations.source: Workplace Fairness, State Laws on Military Leave (50-state survey, used for encoding)
Paycor, Military Leave Laws by State (survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Washington — Military Family Leave (15 days)

params.trigger: spouse notified of an impending call to active duty or on leave from deployment during a period of military conflict

result.summary: All employers must give an employee who works an average of 20 or more hours a week up to 15 days of unpaid leave per deployment when a spouse or domestic partner is called to active duty or is on leave from deployment during a military conflict; employee may elect accrued paid leave; 5 business days' notice.

rules.title: Federal FMLA — Employee Eligibility

result.summary: Employee is FMLA-eligible: entitled to up to 12 weeks unpaid job-protected leave

citations.source: Family and Medical Leave Act, 29 U.S.C. §2612

rules.title: Washington Family & Medical Leave (16 weeks, paid)

result.summary: 16 weeks of paid family and medical leave

rules.title: Washington — Accrued Vacation at Separation (payout per employer policy)

result.summary: Vacation payout follows the employer's policy or agreement; no statutory duty. (Survey-based encoding; dates not researched.)

citations.source: Paycor, PTO Payout Laws by State (survey used for encoding)
Patriot Software, PTO Payout Laws by State (survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Washington — PFML Bereavement Leave (7 days, any family member)

params.covered_relationships: child, spouse, domestic partner, parent, parent-in-law, sibling, grandparent, grandchild

result.summary: From 2026-07-01 (SB 5217, 2025) PFML bereavement leave covers up to 7 days within 12 months of the death of any qualifying family member, paid through the state PFML program.

rules.title: Seattle Paid Sick Leave (1 hr per 30 hrs worked, up to 72 hrs)

result.summary: 72 hours of paid sick leave per year, accrued at 1 hour per 30 hours worked

citations.source: Seattle Paid Sick & Safe Time Ordinance

rules.title: Washington Paid Sick Leave (1 hr per 40 hrs worked, up to 40 hrs/yr)

result.summary: 40 hours of paid sick leave per year, accrued at 1 hour per 40 hours worked

rules.title: Washington — Sick Leave Usage (waiting period, increments)

result.summary: Use may begin on the 90th calendar day of employment; leave is taken in the increments the payroll system uses, no larger than one hour; there is no cap on annual use.

rules.title: Washington — Sick Leave Carryover and Payout

result.summary: Up to 40 hours of unused paid sick leave carries over each year; frontloading does not remove the duty for hours left unused. No payout at separation; balance reinstated on rehire within 12 months.

rules.title: Washington — Minors 14-15: 30-min meal within 4 hours

result.summary: Minors under 16 get an uninterrupted 30-minute meal period beginning before the fourth consecutive hour of work; may not be waived.

rules.title: Washington — Minors 14-15: paid 10-min rest per 2 hours

result.summary: Minors under 16 get a paid 10-minute rest break within every 2 consecutive hours of work, in addition to meal periods.

rules.title: Washington — Minors 16-17: 30-min meal within 5 hours

rules.title: FLSA — Hours Worked Standard

params.notes: Hours worked = time the employee is suffered or permitted to work; the Portal-to-Portal Act excludes ordinary commuting and activities preliminary or postliminary to the principal activity (incl. security screening, Integrity Staffing v. Busk 2014); 29 CFR 785.47 lets insubstantial, irregular minutes be disregarded

result.summary: Under the FLSA all time an employee is suffered or permitted to work is paid, except ordinary commuting and preliminary or postliminary activities excluded by the Portal-to-Portal Act; a de minimis exception exists.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Commute)

result.summary: Ordinary home-to-work travel is not hours worked, even to different worksites, unless the employee works during the trip.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Between Worksites)

result.summary: Travel between job sites during the workday, or from the employer's premises to the first site after reporting, is hours worked.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Special One Day Assignment)

params.notes: Employer may deduct the normal home-to-work commute time

result.summary: A special one-day assignment in another city is hours worked, less the time of the employee's normal commute.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Out Of Town)

result.summary: Overnight travel away from home is hours worked only during the employee's normal working hours (including corresponding hours on non-working days); passenger time outside those hours is unpaid unless work is done.

rules.title: FLSA — Travel Time (Employer Mandated Transport)

result.summary: Riding employer-provided transport from a meeting point to the worksite is not hours worked under the Portal-to-Portal Act unless the travel is itself a principal activity; several states (CA, NY, WA, MD, PA, MA) count it.

rules.title: FLSA — Restricted On-Call Time

params.test: engaged to wait: employee must remain on the premises or so close that the time cannot be used effectively for personal purposes

result.summary: An employee required to stay on or near the premises while on call is working and must be paid.

rules.title: FLSA — Unrestricted On-Call Time

params.test: waiting to be engaged: employee may leave a contact number and use the time for personal purposes
params.notes: Time actually spent responding to calls is paid

result.summary: An on-call employee who need only leave a contact number and can use the time freely is not working; only time responding to calls is paid.

rules.title: FLSA — Mandatory Training and Meetings

params.notes: Attendance is not voluntary if required or if the employee is led to believe non-attendance would hurt their job

result.summary: Required training, orientation and meetings are hours worked.

rules.title: FLSA — Voluntary Training Outside Hours

params.exclusion_test: all four: outside regular hours, genuinely voluntary, not directly related to the employee's current job, and no productive work performed
params.notes: Training to acquire a new or additional skill is not 'directly related'; apprenticeship instruction and independent courses are excluded

result.summary: Training is unpaid only when it is outside regular hours, voluntary, not directly related to the current job and involves no productive work; otherwise it is hours worked.

rules.title: FLSA — Time Clock Rounding

params.notes: Rounding to the nearest 5, 6 or 15 minutes is accepted where it averages out and does not fail to pay for all time actually worked over a period

result.summary: Punches may be rounded to the nearest quarter hour (or smaller increment) if the practice is neutral and does not, over time, fail to pay employees for all hours worked.

rules.title: Washington — Hours Worked Standard

params.notes: Port of Tacoma v. Sacks (Wash. Ct. App. 2021) and Anderson v. DSHS: all work-related travel compensable

result.summary: Washington counts all time the employee is authorized or required to be on duty on the premises or at a prescribed workplace; unlike federal law all out-of-town travel is paid.

citations.source: L&I Administrative Policy ES.C.2, Hours Worked (rev. 2021-07-19)

rules.title: Washington — Travel Time (Out Of Town)

result.summary: All out-of-town travel required for work is hours worked in Washington, including travel to the airport and passenger time outside normal hours; only free time at the destination is unpaid.

citations.source: L&I Administrative Policy ES.C.2, Hours Worked (rev. 2021-07-19)
Port of Tacoma v. Sacks, 19 Wn. App. 2d 295 (2021)

rules.title: Washington — Travel Time (Between Worksites)

result.summary: Travel between worksites during the day, and from a required reporting point to the first site, is hours worked.

citations.source: L&I Administrative Policy ES.C.2, Hours Worked (rev. 2021-07-19)

rules.title: Washington — Time Clock Rounding

result.summary: Neutral rounding to the nearest quarter hour is accepted for shift punches but not for meal or rest periods; a policy that favours the employer in practice is unlawful (Bennett v. Providence, 2025).

citations.source: L&I Administrative Policy ES.C.2, Hours Worked (rev. 2021-07-19)

rules.title: Federal Minimum Wage (FLSA)

result.summary: $7.25 per hour minimum wage

rules.title: Seattle Minimum Wage

result.summary: $20.76 per hour minimum wage

rules.title: Washington State Minimum Wage

result.summary: $16.66 per hour minimum wage

rules.title: Federal Weekly Overtime (FLSA)

result.summary: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 40 in a week

rules.title: Washington State Weekly Overtime (RCW 49.46.130)

result.summary: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 40 in a week

rules.title: Federal Workweek Definition (FLSA)

result.summary: Overtime is computed over a fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) that may begin on any day and hour; it may be changed only permanently and not to evade overtime, and hours may not be averaged across weeks

rules.title: Federal — EAP Exemption Salary Level $684/week (29 CFR 541.600)

result.summary: An executive, administrative or professional employee is exempt from FLSA overtime only if paid on a salary basis at least $684 a week ($35,568 a year), plus $107,432 total annual compensation for the highly compensated employee test. The 2024 rule raising these levels was vacated (E.D. Tex. 2024-11-15) and formally rescinded by DOL on 2026-05-15, so the 2019 levels remain in force. States may set higher thresholds.

rules.title: Washington — Exempt Salary Threshold $1,541.70/week (2.25x Minimum Wage), 2026

params.basis: 2.25 x state minimum wage ($17.13) x 40 hours, all employer sizes

result.summary: Executive, administrative and professional employees are exempt from the Minimum Wage Act only if paid at least 2.25 times the state minimum wage for a 40-hour week in 2026: $1,541.70 a week ($80,168.40 a year), the same for all employer sizes. Exempt computer professionals paid hourly need at least $59.96 an hour. The multiplier reaches 2.5 in 2028.

rules.title: Washington — Pay Frequency

result.summary: Wages must be paid at least monthly on regular paydays, no later than 10 days after the end of the pay period.

rules.title: FLSA — Wage Deductions

result.summary: Under the FLSA, deductions for items that primarily benefit the employer (uniforms, tools, cash shortages, damage) may not reduce pay below the minimum wage or cut into overtime.

citations.source: 29 CFR §531.35 (wages must be paid free and clear)
US DOL Fact Sheet #16: Deductions from Wages for Uniforms and Other Facilities

rules.title: Washington — Wage Deductions

result.summary: During employment deductions need advance written authorization for the employee's benefit, and register shortages, bad checks, walkouts, breakage and lost equipment may never be deducted; only the final paycheck may absorb losses from that pay period caused by the employee's sole access, dishonesty or theft with a police report.

citations.source: Ezel, Employee Wage Deduction Requirements by State (survey)

rules.title: Equal Pay Act of 1963 — Equal Pay

params.notes: Covers all FLSA-covered employers; NLRA §7 separately protects most non-supervisory employees who discuss wages

result.summary: Employees of the opposite sex doing equal work (equal skill, effort and responsibility under similar conditions) in the same establishment must be paid equally unless a seniority, merit, production or other factor-other-than-sex system explains the gap.

rules.title: Washington — Equal Pay

result.summary: Similarly employed workers (same employer, similar job requirements of skill, effort and responsibility under similar conditions) may not be paid differently because of gender unless the gap rests on bona fide job-related factors; wage discussion may not be prohibited.

citations.source: Paycor, Pay Equity and State-by-State Laws (survey)

rules.title: Washington Meal Break (30 min for 5+ hr shift)

result.summary: 30-minute meal break for shifts of 5+ hours

rules.title: Washington — Meal Break Required (shifts > 5 hrs)

result.summary: Washington requires a 30-minute meal break for shifts over 5 hours. Ensure a break is scheduled.

rules.title: Washington — Employees May Waive Meal Periods; On-Duty Meals Are Paid (WAC 296-126-092)

result.summary: An employee may waive the 30-minute meal period (L&I Administrative Policy ES.C.6.1); the employer bears the burden of showing a knowing and voluntary waiver, so a written, revocable waiver is recommended. A meal period during which the employee must remain on duty or on the premises in the employer's interest is paid. In force before 2000.

citations.source: Washington L&I, Rest breaks, meal periods and schedules

rules.title: Seattle — Offer Hours to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or using staffing agencies, the employer must post a notice of available hours for 3 days and offer them to qualified existing employees

rules.title: Seattle — 14-Day Advance Notice Required

result.summary: 1 hour of pay per shift for schedule posted with less than 14 days notice

rules.title: Seattle — Schedule Change Premium (hours or shift added, or time changed, with <14 days notice)

result.summary: 1 additional hour of pay when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer adds hours, adds a shift, or changes the date, time or location of a shift without reducing hours

rules.title: Seattle — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted with <14 days notice)

result.summary: 50% of pay for subtracted/cancelled hours (predictability pay)

rules.title: Seattle — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: At hire the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's expected median hours and whether on-call shifts are expected; it must be revisited yearly and when a significant change occurs

rules.title: Seattle — On-Call Shift Premium (not called in)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour of an on-call shift the employee is not called in to work

rules.title: Seattle — Right to Decline Late-Added Hours

result.summary: The employee may decline any hours or shifts not on the posted schedule or added with less than 14 days notice

rules.title: Seattle — Secure Scheduling: Right to Request Input Into the Schedule

result.summary: Covered employees may request preferences for hours, times and locations at hire and during employment, and the employer must engage in a timely interactive process. A request tied to a major life event (serious health condition, caregiving, education, a second job, or a change in transportation or housing) must be granted unless the employer has a bona fide business reason, stated in writing; other requests may be granted or denied. Employee-requested changes do not trigger predictability pay.

rules.title: Federal Lactation Break Time (PUMP Act)

result.summary: Reasonable break time each time the employee needs to express milk for one year after the child's birth, in a private non-bathroom space; unpaid unless the employee is not fully relieved or uses a paid break (employers under 50 may claim undue hardship)

citations.source: Fair Labor Standards Act §18d (PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act)

rules.title: Washington Lactation Breaks

result.summary: Reasonable break time to express milk, as often as needed, for two years after birth, with a private space; unpaid until 2027-01-01, when paid break time is required

citations.source: Wash. Rev. Code §43.10.005 (Healthy Starts Act) (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Washington Rest Break (10 min per 4 hours worked)

result.summary: 10-minute rest break for shifts of 4+ hours

rules.title: Washington — Rest Break Required (per 4 hrs worked)

result.summary: Washington requires a paid 10-minute rest break for every 4 hours worked. Ensure rest breaks are scheduled.

rules.title: Seattle — 10-Hour Rest Period

result.summary: 1.5x pay rate for hours worked within the 10-hour rest period

rules.title: Washington — Final Wages on Discharge Or Resignation

result.summary: Final wages are due by the end of the established pay period (the next regular payday).

params.name: age_min
params.description: Youngest age covered

params.name: age_max
params.description: Oldest age covered

params.name: max_hours
params.description: Maximum hours in the day

params.name: school_day
params.description: True for school days, false for non-school days; omitted when it applies always

obligations.name: Minor weekly hours limit
obligations.description: Most hours a minor may work in one week.

params.name: age_min
params.description: Youngest age covered

params.name: age_max
params.description: Oldest age covered

params.name: max_hours
params.description: Maximum hours in the week

params.name: school_week
params.description: True for weeks when school is in session, false for non-school weeks; omitted when it applies always

obligations.name: Compensable training and meetings
obligations.description: Whether time in training, lectures, orientation or meetings counts as hours worked.

params.name: compensable
params.description: Whether the time must be paid

params.name: situation
params.description: Whether attendance is required

params.name: exclusion_test
params.description: Conditions under which the time may be unpaid

params.name: expenses_reimbursable
params.description: Whether the employer must also bear the cost of required training

params.name: notes
params.description: Exceptions such as state-mandated licensing courses

obligations.name: Compensable travel time
obligations.description: Whether a kind of travel counts as hours worked.

params.name: compensable
params.description: Whether the travel must be paid

params.name: travel_type
params.description: The travel situation the rule decides

params.name: during_normal_hours_only
params.description: Whether only travel that overlaps the employee's normal working hours (including on non-working days) is paid

params.name: minimum_wage_rate_allowed
params.description: Whether the employer may pay travel at an agreed rate as low as the minimum wage instead of the regular rate

params.name: distance_threshold_miles
params.description: Distance beyond which the travel becomes compensable

params.name: notes
params.description: Exceptions and the governing test

obligations.name: Compensable waiting and on-call time
obligations.description: Whether on-call or waiting time counts as hours worked.

params.name: compensable
params.description: Whether the time must be paid

params.name: situation
params.description: The waiting situation the rule decides

params.name: test
params.description: The legal test applied (engaged to wait vs waiting to be engaged, control test)

params.name: notes
params.description: Exceptions and agreements that change the result

obligations.name: Equal pay
obligations.description: Employees doing the same or comparable work may not be paid differently because of a protected characteristic; some states also protect employees who discuss wages.

params.name: comparison_standard
params.description: How alike two jobs must be for a pay difference to need a lawful justification; discrimination_statute_only means pay bias is reached only through the general anti-discrimination law

params.name: protected_classes
params.description: Characteristics the pay comparison protects

params.name: min_employees
params.description: Employer size at which the law attaches

params.name: pay_secrecy_prohibited
params.description: Whether the state bars employers from forbidding or punishing wage discussions

params.name: notes
params.description: Lawful justifications, remedies and recent amendments

obligations.name: Exempt salary threshold
obligations.description: The lowest weekly salary at which an executive, administrative or professional employee may be treated as exempt from overtime; below it the employee is owed overtime regardless of duties.

params.name: weekly_salary
params.description: Minimum weekly salary for the exemption

params.name: annual_salary
params.description: The same threshold expressed per year

params.name: basis
params.description: How the figure is set (fixed, multiple of the minimum wage, indexed)

obligations.name: Hours-worked standard
obligations.description: Which definition of compensable time governs in the jurisdiction: the FLSA with its Portal-to-Portal exclusions, a state regulation of its own, or a control test that counts any time under the employer's control.

params.name: standard
params.description: flsa_by_reference: the state adopts or defers to 29 CFR 785; state_regulation: the state has its own hours-worked rule (often close to federal but without some exclusions); control_test: any time subject to the employer's control is paid; no_state_law: only the FLSA applies

params.name: portal_to_portal_adopted
params.description: Whether the state excludes ordinary commuting and pre/post-shift activities the way 29 U.S.C. §254 does

params.name: de_minimis_allowed
params.description: Whether small amounts of off-the-clock time may be disregarded

params.name: notes
params.description: Where the state departs from federal law

obligations.name: Pay frequency
obligations.description: How often wages must be paid and how soon after the pay period ends; many states let exempt or salaried staff be paid less often.

params.name: minimum_frequency
params.description: Least frequent lawful pay schedule for the employees the rule covers; none means the state sets no frequency

params.name: max_days_between_paydays
params.description: Longest lawful gap between paydays where the statute counts days

params.name: max_lag_days
params.description: Days after the end of a pay period by which wages for that period must be paid

params.name: lag_business_days
params.description: Whether max_lag_days counts business days only

params.name: exempt_may_be_monthly
params.description: Whether exempt, executive, administrative or professional employees may be paid monthly

params.name: applies_to
params.description: Who the frequency rule covers when narrower than all employees

params.name: notes
params.description: Waivers, agency approvals and other wrinkles

obligations.name: Time clock rounding
obligations.description: Whether punches may be rounded to an increment, and on what conditions.

params.name: permitted
params.description: Whether rounding is lawful at all

params.name: max_increment_minutes
params.description: Largest increment the authority accepts

params.name: neutrality_required
params.description: Whether the policy must round both ways and not under-pay over time

params.name: meal_period_rounding_permitted
params.description: Whether meal-period punches may be rounded

params.name: exact_capture_bars_rounding
params.description: Whether rounding is barred when the system records exact punch times

params.name: notes
params.description: Governing cases and agency guidance

obligations.name: Wage deductions
obligations.description: What an employer may take out of a paycheck beyond taxes and court orders, whether the employee must authorize it in writing, and whether cash shortages, breakage or damage may ever be charged back.

params.name: written_authorization_required
params.description: What the employee must sign (or be told) before a voluntary deduction; not_required means the state has no general consent statute and only the FLSA floor applies

params.name: shortage_damage_deductions
params.description: Whether cash shortages, breakage, lost or damaged property may be deducted and on what condition

params.name: below_minimum_wage_prohibited
params.description: Whether employer-benefit deductions may never reduce pay below the minimum wage

params.name: penalty
params.description: Statutory remedy for an unlawful deduction

params.name: notes
params.description: Caps, timing, revocation and other wrinkles

obligations.name: Workweek and workday definition
obligations.description: The fixed, regularly recurring period over which overtime hours are counted; it may start on any day and hour but cannot be moved to avoid overtime.

params.name: period_hours
params.description: Length of the workweek in hours (168 = seven consecutive 24-hour periods)

params.name: workday_hours
params.description: Length of the workday where daily overtime applies (24 consecutive hours)

params.name: fixed_recurring
params.description: The period must be fixed and regularly recurring; changes are allowed only if permanent and not designed to evade overtime

obligations.name: Overtime premium
obligations.description: A multiple of the regular rate owed for hours past a daily or weekly threshold.

params.name: multiplier
params.description: Multiple of the regular rate (1.5, 2)

params.name: threshold_hours
params.description: Hours after which the premium applies

params.name: period
params.description: Whether the threshold is per workday, per workweek, or applies to hours worked on the seventh consecutive day of the workweek

obligations.name: Schedule change premium
obligations.description: Predictability pay owed when the employer changes a posted schedule inside the notice window.

params.name: amount
params.description: Premium amount, in the unit given

params.name: unit
params.description: How the amount is expressed: hours of pay per affected shift, a flat dollar amount, or a percent of the subtracted hours

params.name: notice_window_days
params.description: Changes made with less than this much notice trigger the premium

params.name: change_type
params.description: Which schedule changes trigger the premium: hours added (incl. added shifts), hours reduced (incl. cancellations and early send-home), a time or location change with no change in hours, an on-call shift the employee was not called in for, or any change

obligations.name: Offer of hours to existing employees
obligations.description: Before hiring new staff or using a staffing agency to cover hours, the employer must offer those hours to existing (part-time) employees.

params.name: offer_window_hours
params.description: How long the offer must stay open to existing employees before the employer may hire (72 hours = 3 days)

params.name: max_part_time_hours
params.description: Weekly hours below which an employee counts as part-time for the offer, where the law sets one

synonyms: offer of work to existing employees

obligations.name: Rest between shifts (clopening)
obligations.description: A closing shift followed by an opening shift with less than the required rest is barred, or owes a premium, unless the employee consents.

params.name: rest_hours
params.description: Minimum hours between the end of one shift and the start of the next

params.name: amount
params.description: Premium amount, in the unit given

params.name: unit
params.description: How the premium is expressed

obligations.name: Good faith estimate of hours
obligations.description: At hire (and on request or when circumstances change) the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's expected hours, days and shifts.

params.name: lookback_days
params.description: Period the estimate is based on or must be revisited over, where the law sets one (Philadelphia and Chicago: 90 days)

obligations.name: Right to decline late-added hours
obligations.description: The employee may refuse hours or shifts the employer adds or moves inside the notice window; working them needs the employee's consent.

params.name: notice_days
params.description: Hours added with less than this much notice may be declined

obligations.name: Right to request schedule changes
obligations.description: The employee may ask for changes to hours, days, times, location or a flexible or predictable arrangement without retaliation; some laws also oblige the employer to consider, answer in writing, or grant the request absent a business reason.

params.name: must_grant_unless_business_reason
params.description: Whether the employer must grant the request unless it has a bona fide business reason or undue hardship (false = consider or respond only)

params.name: written_response_days
params.description: Days the employer has to answer in writing

params.name: requests_per_year
params.description: Requests the employer must entertain per year

params.name: retaliation_only
params.description: True when the law only bars retaliation for asking

obligations.name: Final paycheck deadline
obligations.description: When all wages earned through separation must be paid, which usually differs for a discharge and a resignation.

params.name: deadline
params.description: Shape of the deadline; no_state_law means only the FLSA next-regular-payday practice applies

params.name: hours
params.description: Hours after separation (or after demand) when deadline is within_hours

params.name: days
params.description: Days after separation when the deadline counts days

params.name: business_days
params.description: Whether the day count excludes weekends and holidays

params.name: runs_from_demand
params.description: Whether the clock starts at the employee's demand for payment rather than at separation

params.name: notice_shortens_deadline
params.description: How advance notice from the employee changes the deadline

params.name: penalty
params.description: Statutory penalty for late payment

obligations.name: Minimum wage
obligations.description: The lowest hourly rate an employer may pay a covered employee.

params.name: rate
params.description: Minimum hourly rate
